title.narrative: Third Small Towns Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project

description.narrative: ADB and the Government of Nepal are working together to provide water supply and sanitation services to selected small towns in the country. The Third Small Town Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project is providing the services to small towns with a population of 5,000 to 40,000 that show the potential for growth by having access to roads, power supply and telecommunications. This includes the upgrade or construction of water supply systems in up to 20 small towns, involving 1,450 kilometers of water supply pipelines; 67,500 household connections; and 20 water treatment systems with an estimated capacity of 50,000 cubic meters per day. The project will also provide about 5,000 household toilets with septic tanks, as well as provision of septic management facilities and equipment. Drainage systems and master plans are also prepared in towns with flooding risks. Training is being provided to help local water agencies modernize their operations and manage water rates, and to teach local communities public awareness on water conservation and public hygiene.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Inclusive, genderfocused, and sustainable WSS service delivery in project towns.

By 2020: 390,000 people in project towns have access to 24-hour, 7-day piped water supply at 100 lpcd (including all poor, female headed household, and vulnerable households) (2014 baseline: 19,500 people have piped water 2 hours per day at 45 lpcd.) Achievement: 398871 Progress/Status: Altogether 398,871 (286,403 from 20 new towns, 106,913 from 24 enhancement towns, and 5,555 from enhancement work of additional 12 towns) have now access to water supply facilities. Data Source: (For all indicators) National census; reports by WUAs or local bodies; and project surveys

390,000 people in project towns have access to improved sanitation facilities (including all poor, female headed household, and vulnerable households) (2014 baseline: 288,600 people) Achievement: 398871 Progress/Status: All the people of the project towns have now access to improved sanitation facilities as all the country is already (in September 2019) declared open defecation free. The project also contributed to this as well through output based aid which supported the construction of about 5,000 household toilets. Data Source: National census, reports by PMOs, WUAs or local bodies

Institutional and regulatory framework for WUAs in small towns strengthened through tariff guidelines, corporatization, and management agreements (baseline: none existing) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Tariff guidelines are already updated with the support of ISSAU and TDF. Management agreements are already in place for all small towns. Study on corporatization is ongoing, it will take some time to materialize. Data Source: Financial statements of SEIU, WUAs or local bodies Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

Project towns are declared free of open defecation by the respective water sanitation and hygiene coordination committees (2014 baseline: none declared free of defecation) Achievement: y Progress/Status: All project towns are declared open defecation free. In fact, whole country is declared open defecation free. Data Source: Local water sanitation and hygiene coordination committees' reports Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

Water supplied meets the national drinking water quality standards of 2005 (baseline: noncompliant) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed subprojects are supplying water that meets the National Drinking Water Quality Standards 2005. Data Source: Reports by regional water quality monitoring laboratories, WUAs or local bodies Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

Water supply and sanitation facilities operate at 80% of O&M cost recovery and at least 25% of capital cost recovery (baseline: no cost recovery) Achievement: N Progress/Status: The WS systems which are in operation have set tariff to recover the O&M and debt repayment services except two towns. The local government will support the O&M of these towns. Data Source: Reports of TDF and PMO Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N
